question: Should OpenClaw add `agents.list[].subagents.workspace` for same-agent default child workspace isolation, or keep explicit child agent profiles plus `requireAgentId` as the supported boundary?
rationale: This changes which files default child subagents can access and adds public configuration surface, so automation should not choose the security and compatibility policy.

options.title: Keep explicit profiles
options.body: Preserve the current model where isolation requires configured child agents with their own workspaces and `requireAgentId` for no-default-child enforcement.

options.title: Add opt-in workspace override
options.body: Implement `subagents.workspace` as a strict opt-in same-agent default-child override with schema, docs, and regression/security tests.

options.title: Defer to broader isolation design
options.body: Resolve this together with skill workdir isolation in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87253 so runtime and skill boundaries stay consistent.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit profiles
recommendation.body: Preserve the current model where isolation requires configured child agents with their own workspaces and `requireAgentId` for no-default-child enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available routing candidate from recent subagent/config path history and can choose the product/security boundary.
